description: Our presentation uses an app and suit to incorporate data by allowing astronauts to wear and exercise. The suit will analyze and gather data to send to an app and provide immediate feedback on how to improve an astronaut's physical health. Skills needed are coding, teamwork, and ambition
summary: Our project uses a wetsuit combined with an app to track data on the physical health of astronauts while in space. This will allow astronauts to exercise and see which muscles require exercise and which are being properly maintained. Also, this suit will track muscle atrophy, bone density, and O2 levels while being used. This addresses the challenge of health monitoring systems by addressing the physical fitness of astronauts. Through monitoring their physical health; we can make sure and maintain the health of the astronauts between each visit in space since each visit requires mental and physical retention. We hope to boost the morale of astronauts by giving positive feedback and how their muscles develop of degrade.
details:
What exactly will it do?

ASTRA is an app that will function primarily to track physical health and help retain muscles. Astronauts will wear this suit while exercising, and this will allow the app to gain data on muscle retention, growth, or loss. Ultimately this app functions for the physical health of astronauts to allow better physical recovery after returning to Earth. Additionally, ASTRA will monitor muscle strength and endurance, helping identify early signs of muscle deterioration. This data can help astronauts adjust their exercise routines and maintain better physical health throughout their missions.

How does it work?
The wetsuit will have sensors that track body movement and growth and transfer the data to our app, ASTRA. ASTRA will track data such as muscle atrophy, bone density, and O2 levels. Through the data, our app will provide immediate feedback on which exercises are required and which muscles should be maintained while also providing positive and negative feedback. Additionally, ASTRA will monitor physical progress over time, allowing astronauts to identify areas that need improvement. The app will generate personalized exercise recommendations based on each astronaut's physical condition, helping prevent muscle loss and maintain overall strength. This will ultimately improve astronauts' physical health during space missions and support their recovery after returning to Earth.

What's the benefits?

ASTRA provides many benefits for astronauts during space missions. It makes monitoring their physical health easier by providing real-time information about their bodies. The suit can detect unusual changes in muscle activity, blood pressure, heart rate, and other health measurements, helping astronauts notice potential problems earlier. The app also provides personalized exercise recommendations based on their physical condition and shows which muscles may need more rest and recovery. This helps astronauts maintain their muscle strength, manage their exercise routines, and take better care of their bodies. Overall, ASTRA improves health monitoring, provides faster feedback, and helps astronauts stay healthier during long-term space missions. ASTRA helps astronauts take better care of their bodies, maintain muscle strength, and manage the physical challenges of long-term space missions.

What does it achieve?

The ASTRA suit is designed to keep astronauts healthy during long missions in space. In space, weightlessness and confined spaces cause bones and muscles to weaken, and this damage can become permanent once astronauts return to Earth’s gravity. The ASTRA suit helps prevent that. It is made of a skintight fabric with sensors built in all around it. These sensors keep track of muscle activity, heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature and oxygen level. They send their readings to a small computer in the suit, which passes the data to the ASTRA app. The app studies the readings and watches how they change over time, including whether muscle mass goes up or down during exercise. If it notices anything unusual, it alerts both the astronaut and Mission Control so the problem can be dealt with early. The app also tells the astronaut which muscles need more work and gives health recommendations. By tracking the body this closely, the suit lowers the risk of muscle loss and blood pressure problems, and helps astronauts stay in peak condition for the whole mission.

What was used for this project?

For this project, we used NASA research and scientific data to understand how living in space and experiencing microgravity can affect the human body including things like muscle deterioration, changes in heart rate and blood pressure, oxygen levels, and body-temperature changes. We used the information to decide that these five health measurements were the most important to monitor and why they are important to monitor during long duration space missions. We also researched existing NASA’s technologies and wearable health monitoring to help design and get ideas on where to put the sensors and how the software could work. In addition to NASA research, we used artificial intelligence (AI), including ChatGPT, to help us brainstorm ideas, understand scientific information, research possible technologies, and organize our thoughts. ChatGPT also helped us explain complex topics in simpler terms and develop ideas for how our suit and its companion app could function. We used these tools as a resource to support our research and creativity while making our own decisions about the final design. Using the research already given, we used this data and information to make ASTRA our astronaut health monitoring suit. NASA’s data and information helped us learn what happens to the human body in space and what health problems to look for and monitor while in space. We also used communication and teamwork to share ideas and work together to develop our design.
dataRefs: Counteracting Bone and Muscle Loss in Microgravity
